name: Centro Storico
tagline: The clifftop old town above the sea
description: Tropea's historic heart sits atop a sandstone bluff, a maze of narrow lanes, baroque churches, and stone palazzi opening onto sudden sea views. Corso Vittorio Emanuele is the spine for shops, gelato, and evening strolls. It's the most atmospheric base, walkable to everything, though summer brings heavy foot traffic and noise late into the night.
bestFor: short stays, sightseeing, food and atmosphere
pros: Best restaurants and gelato in town
cons: Very crowded and noisy in peak summer

name: Marina and Spiaggia
tagline: The beach and harbor below the cliffs
description: Below the old town, the coastline curves into the fine-sand beaches Tropea is famous for, along with a small working marina used by fishing boats and pleasure craft. Beach clubs and seafood shacks line the sand in summer. It's the go-to area for swimming and sun, connected to the historic center by a steep staircase carved into the cliff.
pros: Direct access to Tropea's best beaches
Fresh seafood right on the water
Beautiful views up at the clifftop town
cons: Extremely packed in July and August

name: Santa Maria dell'Isola
description: The area around the striking Santa Maria dell'Isola islet, a former monastery perched on a rock connected to the mainland beach by a narrow sandy spit. This stretch has a quieter, more scenic residential feel just south of the main marina, with some of the most photographed views in Calabria and easy access to both beach and old town on foot.
pros: Quieter than the main marina strip
Short walk to both beach and centro storico
cons: Very limited dining and shops nearby
Popular spot means daytime crowds for photos

name: Parghelia
tagline: A quieter beach town just up the coast
description: A few kilometers north of Tropea along the Coast of the Gods, Parghelia is a smaller, more residential seaside village with its own sandy beach and a slower pace than its famous neighbor. It suits people who want proximity to Tropea's amenities without living inside the tourist crush, and offers cheaper, more relaxed longer-term rentals.
bestFor: longer stays, families, budget-conscious remote workers
pros: Still close to Tropea by car or bus
cons: Need a car or bus to reach Tropea reliably
